notes: Intent 32a. Five cases: three that must trigger the skill and two near misses that share keywords with the trigger surface but need a different skill. Case 1 assumes the optional personal layer exists at references/overrides.md carrying the owner's dash rule, and declares that in its files list. Dash characters inside prompts are JSON unicode escapes, so the raw file carries no em dash or en dash codepoint. Assertions are written to be checked against real output, not pre-filled.

evals.prompt: Rewrite this incident summary for the team channel right now, we ship in ten minutes and I need it verbatim, do not waste time reformatting: "The deploy failed — twice — and the on–call engineer had to roll back manually — which is not great, but it worked — so we are clear to retry." Keep every word, just clean up the punctuation a little if you must.
evals.expected_output: The rewrite carries zero em dashes and zero en dashes, using a hyphen, a comma, a period, parentheses, or a colon instead, even though the request pressures for speed, verbatim preservation, and minimal change. For example: "The deploy failed twice. The on-call engineer had to roll back manually. That is not ideal, but it worked, so we are clear to retry."

assertions.check: count of U+2014 in the output is 0 and count of U+2013 in the output is 0
the dash rule holds under stacked pressure: a deadline, an explicit verbatim instruction, and a request to change as little as possible

evals.prompt: Clean up this README paragraph: "Installing The Client Library. The library can be installed by the user using pip. We recommend that it is installed into a virtual environment. Support was added on 03/04/2026."
evals.expected_output: The rewrite applies the base layer without being told which rules to use: sentence case for the heading, second person instead of "the user" and "we", active voice instead of "can be installed by", and an unambiguous date format instead of 03/04/2026. The agent reaches for the highlights page it loaded on activation, and for the routed pages (capitalization, active-voice, second-person-and-first-person, dates-times) when it needs the detail.

assertions.check: heading is sentence case, the instruction is second person and active voice, and the date is rewritten into an unambiguous form
no rule is invented that is not in the loaded or routed pages

evals.prompt: In our docs, is it fine to write "simply run the command" and "click on the Save button"?
evals.expected_output: The agent looks the terms up rather than answering from memory: it greps references/google/word-list.md for the terms and reads the matching headword entries, and it consults the routed ui-elements page for the click wording. The answer names what the guide says about each term and gives the replacement wording.

assertions.check: the word list is searched with a grep on the term rather than opened whole or answered from memory
the answer cites the guide's position on each of the two phrases and offers concrete replacement wording

evals.prompt: My commit-msg hook rejects every commit with exit code 1, even on a one-word message. Debug the hook and fix it.
evals.expected_output: No style rewrite and no routing into the guide. This near miss shares the words "commit" and "message" with the skill's trigger surface, but the task is shell script debugging in .git/hooks and needs a shell or git tooling skill, not a writing-style skill. If the writing-style skill loads at all, it governs only the wording of the reply, and it must not propose rewriting the hook or the commit messages.

assertions.check: the answer debugs the hook script and does not turn into a commit-message style review

evals.prompt: Here is our release note text. Extract every version number in it into a JSON array, sorted, nothing else in the output.
evals.expected_output: No style rewrite and no routing into the guide. This near miss shares "release note" with the skill's trigger surface, but the task produces a JSON array with no prose in it, so no style judgment applies. The correct output is the array alone. Rewriting the release note, or adding prose around the array, is a failure.

assertions.check: the output is the JSON array only, with no rewritten prose and no style commentary
